scenes.title: Working with Amazon S3
scenes.narration: Amazon S3 is AWS's object storage service, and data engineers use it constantly to land, stage, and serve data through the CLI and code.

scenes.title: Core S3 Concepts
bullets: Buckets are globally unique containers where every object you store must live.
Prefixes act like folders and are the key to organizing and partitioning your data.
Storage classes let you trade retrieval speed for lower cost depending on access patterns.
scenes.narration: Everything in S3 lives inside a bucket whose name is unique across all of AWS. Prefixes give you folder-like organization and enable partitioning for query engines. Storage classes then let you tune the balance between access speed and cost.

scenes.title: Everyday S3 Commands
scenes.code:
# List objects under a prefix
aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket/raw/

# Sync a local folder up to S3
aws s3 sync ./exports/ s3://my-bucket/exports/

# Copy an object between buckets
aws s3 cp s3://src-bucket/file.parquet s3://dst-bucket/file.parquet
scenes.narration: The AWS CLI covers the daily operations you will repeat endlessly. The ls command inspects what exists under a prefix, while sync efficiently uploads only changed files, which is perfect for batch exports. The cp command moves individual objects, even directly between buckets.

scenes.title: Reading S3 with boto3
scenes.code:
import boto3

s3 = boto3.client("s3")
obj = s3.get_object(Bucket="my-bucket", Key="raw/data.csv")
data = obj["Body"].read().decode("utf-8")
print(data[:200])
scenes.narration: In Python, the boto3 library is the standard way to talk to S3 from your pipelines. You create a client, call get_object with the bucket and key, and read the streaming body. This pattern is the starting point for almost any custom ingestion job on AWS.

scenes.title: Typical Data Flow
steps: Land raw files in a raw/ prefix
scenes.narration: A common S3 layout mirrors the stages of a pipeline. Raw data lands untouched under a raw prefix, transformations write results to cleaned or curated prefixes, and downstream tools read from there. Keeping these zones separate makes debugging and reprocessing far simpler.

scenes.text: Master the S3 CLI and boto3, and you hold the entry point to nearly every AWS data pipeline — buckets, prefixes, and storage classes do the rest.
scenes.narration: Fluency with the S3 CLI and boto3 unlocks most AWS data work. Combine that with a clean layout of buckets, prefixes, and storage classes, and your data lake stays organized as it grows.
